prediction.likelyOutcome: The court will almost certainly reject both extremes: it will likely discount the claimant's redevelopment-based $1.7M figure heavily for lack of proof that the two-story building was reasonably probable, while also rejecting the State's $56,825 figure as failing to credit the property's actual $225,000/year net lease income and the already-existing, lawful commercial parking use of part of the R-10 parcel. A middle-ground award is likely, probably in the low-to-mid hundreds of thousands of dollars, with the parking-related HBU argument for the R-10 portion being the single most persuasive lever available to the claimant.

outcome.description: After a nonjury trial the Court of Claims largely adopted the State's appraisal (rejecting its 80% discount on the R-10 portion), found direct damages of $71,000 ($54,000 NB portion, $17,000 R-10 portion), and entered judgment for the principal sum of $113,730 including other damages not itemized in the decision. The Appellate Division, Second Department affirmed on May 4, 2022.
